He summoned Chancellor Puyang Xing to the palace and ordered Crown Prince Sun | to come forward and bow to him. The ruler of Wu grasped Xing by the arm, pointed at |, and died. Xing went out and consulted the ministers, intending to enthrone Crown Prince Sun |. Wan Yu, General of the Left of the Central Army, said, “| is too young to govern in his own right. It would be better to bring in Sun Hao, Marquis of Wucheng, and enthrone him.” Zhang Bu, General of the Left, also said, “Hao is talented, discerning, and decisive. He is fit to be an emperor.” Chancellor Puyang Xing could not decide and went in to report to Empress Dowager Zhu. The empress dowager said, “I am merely a widowed woman. p.src: Hao’s courtesy name was Yuanzong. He was the son of Sun He, crown prince of the Great Emperor Sun Quan. In the seventh month of that year, he ascended the imperial throne and proclaimed the first year of Yuanxing. He enfeoffed Crown Prince Sun | as Prince of Yuzhang, posthumously honored his father He as Emperor Wen, elevated his mother Lady He to empress dowager, and appointed Ding Feng Grand Marshal of both the Left and the Right. The following year he changed the era name to the first year of Ganlu. Hao grew more savage and violent by the day, abandoned himself cruelly to wine and women, and favored the palace attendant Cen Hun. Puyang Xing and Zhang Bu remonstrated with him. Enraged, Hao beheaded them both and exterminated their three clans. Thereafter the court ministers sealed their lips and dared not remonstrate again. He later changed the era name to the first year of Baoding and appointed Lu Kai and Wan Yu chancellors of the Left and Right. At the time Hao resided in Wuchang, and the people of Yangzhou suffered greatly from having to transport supplies upstream. p.src: When the memorial was presented, Hao was displeased. He also embarked on vast building works, constructing the Zhaoming Palace and ordering civil and military officials alike into the mountains to fell timber. He then summoned the diviner Shang Guang and ordered him to consult the yarrow stalks about conquering the realm. Shang replied, “Your Majesty’s divination has yielded an auspicious sign: in the gengzi year, the imperial carriage beneath its blue canopy shall enter Luoyang.” Hao was delighted and said to Hua He, Assistant Director of the Secretariat, “The late emperor accepted your counsel, appointed commanders to separate sectors, established several hundred camps all along the river, and placed the veteran general Ding Feng in overall command. I wish to annex the lands of Han and avenge the ruler of Shu. What place should I take first?” Hua He remonstrated, “Now Chengdu has fallen and the state of Shu has collapsed; Sima Yan is certain to harbor the ambition of swallowing Wu. Your Majesty should cultivate virtue and bring peace to the people of Wu. That is the best policy. If you insist on mobilizing the army, it will be like wearing hemp to fight a fire: you will surely burn yourself. I beg Your Majesty to consider this.” Hao flew into a rage. “I intend to seize this opportunity to restore our former dominion, yet you utter these ill-omened words! Were it not for your standing as an old minister, I would behead you as a warning to all!” He shouted for the guards to thrust him out through the palace gate. Leaving the court, Hua He sighed, “Alas, these splendid rivers and mountains will soon belong to another!” He then withdrew into seclusion and appeared no more at court. Hao then ordered Lu Kang, General Who Guards the East, to station his troops at the river mouth and plot the capture of Xiangyang.

p.src: News of this had already reached Luoyang. An attendant reported it to Sima Yan, ruler of Jin. On hearing that Lu Kang was threatening Xiangyang, the ruler of Jin consulted his officials. Jia Chong stepped forward and memorialized, “I hear that Sun Hao of Wu neither cultivates virtue nor practices good government, but commits nothing save wickedness. Your Majesty may command Governor Yang Hu to lead troops against him, wait until disorder arises within his realm, and then seize the opportunity to attack. Eastern Wu will be as easily won as turning one’s palm.” Yan was delighted. He at once issued an edict and sent an envoy to Xiangyang to convey his command to Yang Hu. Yang Hu received the edict, mustered his troops and horses, and prepared to meet the enemy. From then on, Yang Hu guarded Xiangyang and won the wholehearted support of soldiers and civilians alike. Whenever men of Wu surrendered and wished to return, he allowed them to go. He reduced the number of garrison and patrol troops and employed them to cultivate more than eight hundred qing of farmland. When he first arrived, the army had less than a hundred days’ provisions. By the following year, the army had amassed stores sufficient for ten years. While in the army, Yang Hu habitually wore a light fur robe with a loose sash and no armor; no more than a dozen guards attended before his tent.

p.src: One day, a subordinate commander entered his tent and reported, “The scouts report that the Wu troops are all off their guard. If we take advantage of their unpreparedness and launch a surprise attack, we are certain to win a great victory.” Yang Hu laughed. “Do you all underestimate Lu Kang? That man is resourceful and full of stratagems. Not long ago, the ruler of Wu ordered him to capture Xiling; he slew Bu Chan and scores of his officers and men before I could rescue them. So long as he commands their forces, we can do no more than defend ourselves. Only when internal disorder arises may we seek to take their land. To advance rashly without judging the times and circumstances would be the road to defeat.” The generals accepted his reasoning and merely defended the frontier.

p.src: One day, Yang Hu led his generals out hunting, just as Lu Kang also happened to be hunting. Yang Hu gave the order, “Our troops are not to cross the border.” Obeying the order, the generals conducted the hunt only on Jin territory and did not trespass into Wu. Seeing this from afar, Lu Kang sighed, “General Yang’s troops are disciplined; they must not be provoked.” At sunset, both sides withdrew. After Yang Hu returned to camp, he examined the game that had been taken and sent back every animal previously wounded by a Wu arrow. The men of Wu were all delighted and went to report this to Lu Kang. Kang summoned the messenger and asked, “Can your commander drink wine?” The man replied, “He drinks when he can obtain a fine vintage.” Kang laughed. “I have a dou of wine that I have stored for a long time. I shall entrust it to you now. Take it and present my respects to the governor. It is wine that I, Lu, brewed with my own hands for my own drinking. I specially offer him a measure of it to express the fellowship of yesterday’s hunt.” The messenger accepted the command and departed with the wine. Those around Kang asked, “General, what is your purpose in giving wine to the enemy?” Kang replied, “Since he has shown us kindness, how can I fail to repay it?” All were astonished.

p.src: Now the messenger returned to Yang Hu and recounted in full Lu Kang’s inquiry and his gift of wine. Yang Hu laughed. “So he too knows that I can drink?” He then ordered the jar opened and poured himself a drink. His subordinate general Chen Yuan said, “There may be treachery in it. Governor, you should refrain from drinking for the present.” Yang Hu laughed. “Kang is not one to poison another. There is no need for suspicion.” And he drained the jar to the last. From then on, they sent messengers to exchange greetings and maintained constant contact.

p.src: One day, Lu Kang sent a man to inquire after Yang Hu. Yang Hu asked, “Is General Lu well?” The messenger replied, “My commander has been confined to bed by illness for several days and has not appeared.” Yang Hu said, “I expect his illness is the same as mine. I have here a prepared medicine already compounded. You may take it to him to swallow.” The messenger took the medicine back to Lu Kang. The generals said, “Yang Hu is our enemy. This medicine cannot possibly be wholesome.” Kang replied, “Could Yang Shuzi ever be a man who poisons others? You must not be suspicious.” He then took the medicine. The next day he recovered, and all his generals bowed and congratulated him. Kang said, “He acts solely through virtue, while I act solely through force. Thus he means to subdue me without battle. For now, we should each merely preserve our own borders and not contend for petty gains.” The generals received his command.

p.src: Suddenly it was reported that the ruler of Wu had sent an envoy. Lu Kang received him and asked his business. The envoy said, “The Son of Heaven commands you to advance with all haste and not let the men of Jin enter first.” Lu Kang replied, “Return ahead of me. I shall soon submit a memorial.” After the envoy took his leave, Lu Kang immediately drafted a memorial and sent a man to carry it to Jianye. A close attendant presented it. Sun Hao opened and read the memorial, which explained fully why Jin could not yet be attacked. It also urged the ruler of Wu to cultivate virtue, exercise care in punishment, and make domestic peace his concern instead of pursuing incessant warfare. When the ruler of Wu finished reading, he flew into a rage. “I heard that Lu Kang was communicating with the enemy on the frontier. Now it proves true!” He therefore sent an envoy to strip Lu Kang of military command and demote him to major, while ordering General of the Left Sun Ji to take charge of his army instead. None of the ministers dared remonstrate. From the time the ruler of Wu, Sun Hao, changed the era name to Jianheng until the first year of Fenghuang, he acted wantonly, exhausting the state with warfare and garrisons, and all above and below lamented and resented him. Chancellor Wan Yu, General Liu Ping, and Minister of Agriculture Lou Xuan saw that Sun Hao had abandoned the Way and remonstrated bitterly and frankly; all three were put to death. Over the course of more than ten years, he killed over forty loyal ministers. Whenever Sun Hao went abroad, he was accompanied by fifty thousand armored cavalry. The ministers lived in terror and could do nothing.

p.src: Sima Yan read the memorial and was delighted, at once ordering the army mobilized. Jia Chong, Xun Xu, and Feng Chun argued vehemently against it, so Sima Yan abandoned the expedition. When Yang Hu learned that the emperor had denied his request, he sighed, “Eight or nine of every ten affairs under Heaven go contrary to one’s wishes. Now Heaven grants us an opportunity, yet we do not seize it. What a grievous pity!” In the fourth year of Xianning, Yang Hu entered the court and requested leave to return home and nurse his illness. Sima Yan asked, “What policy have you for securing the realm with which to instruct me?” Yang Hu replied, “Sun Hao’s tyranny has become extreme. At present Wu may be conquered without a battle. But if Sun Hao should happen to die and a worthy sovereign be installed in his place, Wu will lie beyond Your Majesty’s power to obtain.” Sima Yan suddenly understood. “What if you were now to take command and march against Wu?” Yang Hu replied, “I am old and much afflicted by illness; I cannot bear this responsibility. Your Majesty need only choose another man of wisdom and courage.” He then took leave of Sima Yan and returned home. In the eleventh month of that year, Yang Hu became gravely ill, and Sima Yan personally drove to his home to inquire after him. When Sima Yan came to his bedside, Yang Hu wept and said, “Though I die ten thousand deaths, I cannot repay Your Majesty!” Sima Yan also wept. “I regret that I could not adopt your proposal to conquer Wu. Who can now carry on your purpose?” With tears in his eyes, Yang Hu answered, “I am about to die, so I dare not fail to offer the last of my humble sincerity. General of the Right Du Yu is capable of the task. If Your Majesty wishes to conquer Wu, you must employ him.” Sima Yan said, “Promoting the good and recommending the worthy is a noble deed. Why, whenever you recommend someone at court, do you burn your memorial’s draft and let no one know?” Yang Hu replied, “Appointments are made at the public court, but gratitude is offered at a private gate. That is something I will not accept.” With those words, he died. Sima Yan wept bitterly and returned to the palace, decreeing that Yang Hu be posthumously invested as Grand Tutor and Marquis of Juping. When the people of the southern provinces heard that Yang Hu was dead, they closed their markets and wept. The soldiers guarding the frontier along the southern Yangtze also wept. Remembering how Yang Hu had often visited Mount Xian in his lifetime, the people of Xiangyang built a shrine and erected a stele there, making offerings to him in every season. p.src: The ruler of Jin had only just finished reading the memorial when Zhang Hua sprang up, pushed aside the go board, folded his hands, and said, “Your Majesty is sagacious and martial, the state is wealthy, and the people are strong. The ruler of Wu is depraved and cruel; his people are distressed and his state exhausted. If we attack him now, the realm may be settled with little effort. I beg Your Majesty not to hesitate.” The ruler of Jin said, “Your words penetrate every advantage and danger. What further doubt can I have?” He immediately went out and ascended the audience hall. He appointed Senior General Who Pacifies the South Du Yu supreme commander and ordered him to lead one hundred thousand troops from Jiangling; Senior General Who Guards the East, Sima Zhou, Prince of Langya, was to march from Chuzhong; Senior General Who Conquers the East Wang Hun was to march from Hengjiang; General Who Establishes Might Wang Rong was to march from Wuchang; General Who Pacifies the South Hu Fen was to march from Xiakou; each was to lead fifty thousand troops, all subject to Du Yu’s direction. He also sent Dragon-Soaring General Wang Jun and General of Expansive Might Tang Bin to sail eastward down the Yangtze. p.src: Now Du Yu, the Jin commander, marched out from Jiangling. He ordered his subordinate officer Zhou Zhi to lead eight hundred sailors across the Yangtze by stealth in small boats and make a night attack on Lexiang. They planted numerous banners throughout the wooded hills, firing cannon and beating drums by day and lighting fires everywhere by night. Zhou Zhi accepted the order, led his men across the river, and lay in ambush at Mount Ba. The next day, Du Yu led the main army forward by both land and water. A scout reported, “The ruler of Wu has sent Wu Yan by land and Lu Jing by water, with Sun Xin as vanguard. They are advancing along three routes to meet us.” Du Yu led his troops onward. Sun Xin’s fleet arrived first. At the first clash of the two armies, Du Yu immediately retreated. Sun Xin led his troops ashore and pursued them steadily. Before they had gone twenty li, a cannon sounded and Jin troops surged in from every side, forcing the men of Wu to turn back in haste. Du Yu seized the advantage and fell upon them, killing more Wu soldiers than could be counted. When Sun Xin fled back to the city, Zhou Zhi’s eight hundred men mingled with his troops and raised fires upon the walls. Sun Xin cried out in terror, “The armies from the north must have flown across the river!” As he hurried to retreat, Zhou Zhi gave a mighty shout and struck him down beneath his horse. From his ship, Lu Jing saw flames rising all along the southern bank. On Mount Ba, the wind unfurled a great banner inscribed: “Du Yu, Senior General Who Guards the South of Jin.” Lu Jing was terrified and tried to flee ashore for his life, but the Jin general Zhang Shang rode up and slew him. Seeing every army defeated, Wu Yan abandoned the city and fled, but troops lying in ambush captured him, bound him, and brought him before Du Yu. Du Yu said, “There is no use in keeping him alive!” He ordered the guards to behead him. Thus Jiangling was taken. Thereupon, throughout the region of the Yuan and Xiang rivers and as far as the commanderies of Huangzhou, the governors and magistrates submitted at the mere rumor of his approach, bringing their official seals with them. Du Yu sent envoys bearing credentials to pacify the people and forbade his soldiers to take so much as a hair. He then advanced to attack Wuchang. Wuchang also surrendered.

Tao Jun memorialized, “The warships under my command are all small. This is what is meant by the saying: “The great course of the realm is this: after long unity it must divide, and after long division it must unite.”
